newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-LIONS BOSS COTTON BLASTS RFU.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-LIONS BOSS COTTON BLASTS RFU.

text.p: Fran Cotton, manager of the British Lions, attacked the English Rugby Football Union (RFU) on Wednesday, saying they mishandled television negotiations and misled members.

Just 10 days before the Lions set off to tour South Africa, Cotton accused the RFU of selling out to satellite TV company BSkyB, which paid 87.5 million pounds ($143.1 million) for the rights to domestic and international matches for the next five years.
Cotton, a former England international and a British Lion who is president of the independent RFU Reform Group, issued a statement which said: "We know the AGM was misled on several issues.
"We can't have these people thinking they can lie and get away with it. The secretary and those who condone these actions should resign immediately."
Cotton's attack is the latest in a long-standing dispute which has bedevilled the game since it turned professional in 1995.
The RFU denied Cotton's accusations and a spokesman said on Wednesday: "He is unnecessarily creating divisions in the game. His decisions are completely unjustified." ($ = 0.611 British Pounds)
